topics.title: Ukraine diplomacy returns to Kyiv
topics.summary: U.S. envoys held talks in Kyiv aimed at reviving Ukraine peace efforts, with security guarantees, energy resilience, and reconstruction questions still central.
topics.discussionPrompt: If a peace team showed up after months of stalemate, what question would the studio ask first before getting hopeful?

topics.title: Asian chip shares rally
topics.summary: Markets were mixed Monday, but chipmakers lifted Tokyo and Seoul as AI hardware demand kept investors interested despite oil and rate worries.
topics.discussionPrompt: Who in the studio would understand chip stocks, and who would just ask why every gadget suddenly feels more expensive?

topics.title: Oil worries follow Gulf tension
topics.summary: Oil prices climbed as U.S.-Iran clashes around Gulf shipping routes kept traders focused on fuel costs, inflation, and possible knock-on effects.
topics.discussionPrompt: If oil prices jump after a tense headline, who starts planning errands and who insists it is too soon to panic?

topics.title: North Korea adds destroyer
topics.summary: North Korea commissioned a second advanced destroyer as the U.S., South Korea, and Japan began a joint military exercise nearby.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a military parade and a military drill happen at the same time, how does everyone avoid reading too much into one day?

topics.title: AI rules hit classrooms
topics.summary: Major school districts are tightening AI use for younger students, while teachers and parents debate safety, cheating, tutoring, and critical thinking.
topics.discussionPrompt: Would the studio ban classroom AI, teach everyone how to use it, or invent a hilariously complicated permission slip?

topics.title: Unions confront AI at work
topics.summary: Labor unions are increasingly bargaining over AI tools, from health-care staffing software to job security and worker oversight concerns.
topics.discussionPrompt: If a workplace AI promised efficiency, what rule would the studio want in writing before anyone trusted it?

topics.title: Air quality gains face setbacks
topics.summary: A WMO report says heatwaves and wildfire smoke are undoing some air-quality progress, linking climate change more tightly with everyday breathing risks.
topics.discussionPrompt: What would make smoky-sky days feel less abstract: health advice, better alerts, or someone finally fixing the office air filter?

topics.title: Exoplanet survives dead star
topics.summary: Researchers studied a Jupiter-like planet that endured its star's transformation into a white dwarf, offering clues about long-term planetary survival.
topics.discussionPrompt: If a planet can outlast its own sun, who in the studio turns that into science wonder and who makes it weirdly personal?

topics.title: Midterms enter final stretch
topics.summary: Candidates used Labor Day events to sharpen midterm messages, with Senate and governor races drawing attention as early voting nears in some states.
topics.discussionPrompt: Why does Labor Day make campaigns feel like someone rang a bell, even when everyone was already campaigning?

topics.title: Streaming week gets crowded
topics.summary: New picks this week include The Paper, Call My Agent!, music releases, and a Halloween game as fall entertainment schedules fill up.
topics.discussionPrompt: If everyone in the studio got one pick for the watchlist, who chooses comfort TV and who chooses chaos gaming?
